images.title: A day on one strip
images.purpose: Show the whole day as one strip of 24 hour boxes, 00 to 23, with the a.m. side and the p.m. side, and 07:45 p.m. marked in box 19 as 19:45 hours.
images.composition: A caption at the top, an a.m. bar and a p.m. bar over a strip of 24 numbered boxes, a marker under box 19 with its two names, and the addition written large at the bottom.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. TOP LEFT: the caption A day has 24 hours in dark #1F2937 sans-serif bold (40 px), left edge at x 128, about y 60. BANNER: two bars side by side, y 150 to 200. The a.m. bar spans x 128 to 728, filled amber #E69F00 with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline, with a small sun (a dark #1F2937 circle 28 px across with 8 short rays) at x 345 and the text a.m. centred at x 440 in dark bold (36 px). The p.m. bar spans x 728 to 1328, filled teal #0072B2 with the same outline, with a small white crescent moon (28 px) at x 945 and the text p.m. centred at x 1040 in white bold (36 px). STRIP: exactly 24 boxes in one row directly under the bars, each box 50 px wide and 90 px high (y 200 to 290), from x 128 to x 1328, filled white with a dark #2B2B2B outline (2 px). Each box has its hour number centred inside it, from 00 at the left to 23 at the right, in dark bold (26 px): 00, 01, 02, up to 23. The first 12 boxes (00 to 11) sit under the a.m. bar and the last 12 boxes (12 to 23) under the p.m. bar. Exactly 2 boxes are filled reddish purple #CC79A7 instead of white: box 07 (x 478 to 528) and box 19 (x 1078 to 1128); their numbers stay dark. ENDS: a short dark tick (3 px, 30 px long) hangs from the strip at x 128 and at x 1328 (y 290 to 320), with the labels 00:00 centred under the left tick and 24:00 centred under the right tick at about y 345 (30 px, bold, dark). MARKER: one reddish purple #CC79A7 triangle pointing up, its tip touching the bottom of the strip at x 1115, y 290, its base 26 px wide at y 330 (x 1102 to 1128). Under it, centred at x 1115, the label 07:45 p.m. at about y 400 and the label 19:45 hours at about y 455, both in dark bold (40 px). BOTTOM: centred at x 728 and about y 640, one line of bold dark text, 7 + 12 = 19 (80 px), the largest text in the frame. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
more or fewer than 24 boxes, or boxes numbered in any other way than 00 to 23 from left to right
any box filled purple other than box 07 and box 19, or the marker in any box other than box 19
images.takeaway: 07:45 p.m. is 19:45 hours: a p.m. time adds 12 to the hour, 7 + 12 = 19, and the minutes stay 45.
images.description: A strip of 24 hour boxes from 00 to 23 with an a.m. side and a p.m. side, a marker at 07:45 p.m. in box 19 labelled 19:45 hours, and 7 + 12 = 19 written below.
images.context: Concept image for Two Ways to Write the Time. It follows the idea of the 24-hour clock in your maths book (a day counted once from 00:00 to 24:00, with p.m. times 12 hours further on) and shows the concept's own example of 07:45 p.m.
images.teaching_notes: Point first at box 07, then at box 19, and say that the p.m. hour is 12 more. The slip to watch: writing 07:45 p.m. as 07:45 hours, which is a morning time.

image_decisions.why: The strip of the whole day shows that a p.m. time sits 12 hours further along than its morning twin, which is the whole rule.
